/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 05 June 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2981 (-56)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4893 (-147)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2236 (-18)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1588 (4)
Baltic Handysize Index: 864 (2)
CAPESIZE
The market closed the day on a softer note, with the BCI 182 5TC declining by $1,333 to $44,374, reflecting continued pressure across both basins. C5 eased by $0.615 to $13.920, while C3 slipped marginally by $0.132 to $36.50, with both routes lacking fresh momentum as the week drew to a close. Pacific sentiment remained weaker, with a subdued tone prevailing and limited resistance to the ongoing downward drift. In the Atlantic, conditions were broadly steady, although activity was notably thin as participants wound down for the week. Miner presence was minimal, with only one C5 miner active in the market today, contributing to the softer undertone. With limited enquiry, fixing activity remained light. By the close, reports indicated $13.80 being paid on C5, while C3 was last seen at $36.50. Overall, the market ended on a subdued footing with limited trading interest.
PANAMAX
The Atlantic market ended the week on a steadier footing, with brokers noting an improved volume of mineral and grain enquiry, matched by a tonnage list sufficiently ample to absorb demand. Fronthaul activity reflected a similar dynamic, with forward dates continuing to attract interest, although prompt supply remains under pressure. In contrast, the Pacific market remains softer, with sentiment weakening as Australian and Indonesian export volumes have eased compared to recent weeks. Market sources indicate that owners with prompt tonnage are having to discount from previous levels to secure coverage, although some degree of resistance persists.Periods activity was limited, but the BH Power (82,103 2024) open in Cailan 9/15 June was reported to have fixed for two laden legs redelivery Singapore-Japan around $25,000 The P5TC fell by $164 to conclude the week at $20,121.

Asia
The Sakizaya Unicorn (82,516 2021) open Zhuhai 8/9 June was said to have fixed for an Australia round trip in the mid $20,000s with Lotus. While the Golden Lion (84,967 2023) open CJK 7 June fixed for an Australia round with redelivery Japan around $26,000 to MOL. The Samatan (77,154 2015) is also reported fixed from Hong Kong 12 June for an Australia round, though further details remain undisclosed.
SUPRAMAX
After the weeklong shipping events in Athens with many players slowly returning to their desks, unsurprisingly it was a rather slow end to the week. Brokers said that fundamentally changed little and rates general held steady in most areas. The Atlantic saw little fresh information surface and most players looking toward next week to see if the overall positive sentiment continues. From Asia, the WW Nadia (63,250 2012) open Weda 10 June was heard fixed at $25,000 for an Indonesia round redelivery SE Asia with coal to Pan Ocean. A 62,000 open Gresik was also heard fixed via Kalimantan trip redelivery Bangladesh at $28,000 but no more details came to light. Also backhaul was seen, the Kraken (56,830 2011) open Zhoushan 10/11 June was rumoured fixed at $17,000 for a trip to the Continent with Chinaland. the 11TC average finished the week up slightly by $47 at $20,067.
HANDYSIZE
It was a typically quiet Friday for the Handy sector, with minimal visible activity. The Baltic Handysize Index settled at 864, while the 7TC average increased by $38 to close at $15,546. In the Continent and Mediterranean, market fundamentals and rate levels remained largely unchanged. In the South Atlantic, the outlook continued to appear soft due to a lengthy tonnage list and limited demand. Meanwhile, the US Gulf appeared subdued, with no meaningful change in fundamentals. In the Pacific, the market saw a slower day, although owners were willing to wait as rates continued to trend upwards. A 39,000 open in CJK was heard fixed for a trip to East Coast India at $19,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Crude Steel Production

Daily crude steel production at Chinese Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills fell 4.3% from the preceding ten days to 2.0 Mt/day in the period 20-31 May, according to the industry association. Meanwhile, output stood 4.1% below the same period last year. Major still mills’ inventory declined 15.7% from the preceding ten days to 15.83 Mt in late-May.

Trading Commentary
Cape
A day of mixed sentiment for Cape FFA, starting out the blocks softer with Jun sold down to lows of $38650. Despite a negative index print of -1,333, the afternoon session parred the mornings losses as more buyers stepped in, leaving the curve closing in the green across the board. Jun was valued at flat to opening levels at $39100 at the close. Jul traded down to lows of $32350 before being bid up to $32850 at close. Aug closed at $31300 with lows of $30850. Q3 traded $32300-$31500, closing at $32200. Q4 closed at $31500 with lows of $31150. The calendar strips were inactive.

PMX
PMX paper finished the week trading firmer through the session with strength developing across the front end and into the quarters. Jun was the main focus, opening at 20,700 before finding buying interest in the afternoon, being paid up to 21,550 and finishing around 21,300. Jul followed a similar pattern, initially trading down to 21,100 before rallying throughout the day, printing at highs of 21,700 late in the day. Q3 opened around 20,700 and briefly traded down to 20,600 before recovering steadily through the afternoon, trading up to 21,100 into the close. Q4 followed, trading up to 19,600 late on. Further out, Cal 27 saw significant volume throughout the session with repeated clips trading at 15,500, while Cal 28 traded at 14,500.

SMX + HANDY
SMX paper pushed higher through the day. Jun opened around 18,300 before gradually recovering through the day, trading up to 18,600 by the close. Jul, initially traded down to 18,850 before pushing higher, reaching 19,250 and settling back around 19,100. Q3 was the main focus, trading in a 18,600-18,900 range, with repeated clips printing at 18,900 into the close. Q4 also improved, trading from early lows around 17,300 up to 17,500 late in the session. The Q3+Q4 strip was active throughout the day, trading from 17,850 early up to 18,100 later in the session. Further back, Cal 27 traded at 13,650 before improving to 13,675 by the close.

Carbon
EU ETS futures extended their decline from mid-week, with the Dec26 contract falling 0.
